item.title: 'Gaza will be rebuilt': Trump expresses optimism over Israel-Hamas ceasefire; will set up a 'board of peace'
item.description: US President Donald Trump expressed optimism for the Israel-Hamas ceasefire, anticipating Gaza's rebuilding with Arab funding and the establishment of a "Board of Peace." He highlighted the significant retribution against Hamas and the widespread desire for peace across the Middle East, calling the deal beneficial for all.

item.title: Explosion at US military explosives plant: Multiple dead, several missing in Tennessee blast; homes shake miles away
item.description: A powerful explosion rocked a military explosives manufacturing facility in rural Tennessee on Friday morning, causing homes to shake and prompting an emergency response. Officials urged the public to stay clear as ongoing blasts prevented access to the site, with no immediate confirmation of casualties. Footage showed burning debris and smoke rising from the facility near Bucksnort.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE bans Iranian 'Uranus Star' bottled water after two die from contamination in Oman; confirms no permits issued
item.description: After two deaths in Oman linked to contaminated Uranus Star bottled water from Iran, the UAE has barred its import and trade. The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment confirmed no permits were issued and the product isn’t sold locally. Authorities are reviewing import records and have urged the public to avoid and dispose of the brand immediately.

item.title: Donald Trump’s Nobel Snub: The prize he cannot threaten or buy – and what next
item.description: This year’s outcome surprised no one. From Oslo insiders to Washington pundits, the verdict was always the same: Trump was never going to win. The Nobel Peace Prize, for all its hypocrisies, is meant to honour those who “advance fraternity among nations” — those who build peace through cooperation, diplomacy, and trust.

item.title: Etihad Airways lands in Ethiopia with new daily flights connecting Abu Dhabi to Addis Ababa
item.description: Etihad Airways has relaunched daily flights between Abu Dhabi and Addis Ababa, marking a significant expansion into the African market. This new service, operated in partnership with Ethiopian Airlines, aims to boost tourism and trade by offering enhanced connectivity across the Middle East, Africa, and Asia.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Saudi Arabia bans tobacco shops within 500 meters of mosques and schools, imposes strict retail and licensing rules
item.description: Saudi Arabia has introduced strict regulations on tobacco sales, including bans on tobacco shops near mosques and schools, mandatory licensing, and compliance with safety standards. The rules prohibit sales to minors, promotions, and unapproved packaging. Retailers must meet operational and design standards, with municipalities enforcing compliance through penalties and educational signage to improve public health and safety.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Etihad Airways to start 3 weekly flights to Afghanistan on Abu Dhabi-Kabul route from Dec 18, 2025
item.description: Etihad Airways will start new flights to Kabul, Afghanistan from December 18, 2025. This route will operate three times weekly. The flights aim to meet growing travel demand and boost trade. This expansion strengthens connections between the UAE and Afghanistan. It also offers seamless onward travel to global destinations. Etihad is increasing its network significantly.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE telecom giant e& offers 2GB free data for fans traveling to Doha for World Cup qualifiers
item.description: UAE's national football team is gearing up for crucial World Cup qualifiers in Doha against Oman and Qatar. To boost fan support, telecom giant e& is offering free roaming data, while the UAE Football Association has arranged private jet transport for supporters.

item.title: 'He deserved it': Netanyahu, Putin speak out in support of Donald Trump after Nobel Peace Prize snub; Maria Corina Machado named winner
item.description: Venezuelan activist Maria Corina Machado secured the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize for her fight against dictatorship. This decision drew sharp criticism from leaders like Netanyahu and Putin, who felt Donald Trump deserved the award for his peace efforts, particularly in the Middle East. The Nobel Committee, however, maintained its selection was made prior to recent developments.
